reviews.text: I have used Sony noise-cancelling headphones for at least 20 years. I swore by them, despite trying cheaper competitors. Most significantly, the “Speak-to-Chat” function has, for years, frustrated me. But I used to always be able to disable it, whether it was the tap-input or the app settings. But nothing I seem to be able to do any more works. Instead, every 5 minutes my listening is interrupted, and there’s nothing I can do to prevent it. Next time, I’m buying a cheap Chinese competitor who does NOT have the stupid app that constantly gets in the way of the hardware working.

reviews.title: Great Speakers, Pathetic App
reviews.text:
Sony is one of the best and most innovative audio manufacturers—or at least it used to be. Unfortunately, the Sony Sound Connect app is terrible.

I first used it last year with my iPhone 15 Pro Max and the ULT Field 7. After just one day, I returned the speaker. Now I've bought the ULT Field 3. The speaker itself is great, but sadly the app is still just as bad.

The app downloaded the latest firmware, but it won't transfer the update to the speaker because it claims the battery level is too low. The speaker is fully charged (100%) and is connected to the charger, yet the app still refuses to update it.

Sony makes excellent speakers, but the software seriously lets them down.

reviews.title: 3 key flaws and one is a nuisance
reviews.text: This app is fine. It does what it is supposed to for the most part but there are a few issues and one is a near constant nuisance. Firstly, and least impactful, I don’t want this app to sell me anything because I already bought at least one product or I wouldn’t be there to begin with so it is annoying but not unusual that Sony would use my presence as an opportunity to shill their portfolio of related devices and services. Secondly, it is disappointing that the custom EQ setup is literally subjective instead of being remotely scientific. This is a good opportunity to perform an empirical hearing analysis but instead the user is basically asked what genre and vibe they are most interested in. Finally, and this is the biggest gripe I have, it’s great that you can connect to 2 devices at a time. It works well once connects BUT if you need to switch secondary devices (from a TV to a laptop for instance), you can’t just tap on another device in your list of paired options. Instead you will get an error telling you that you must first disconnect from the device you are presently connected to and THEN you can connect to a new one. Apps for headphones from other manufacturers (Sennheiser for instance) do this seamlessly; when you tap on a different device, you get disconnected from the current device and reconnected to the new one without any further discussion. I have to switch secondary devices on a regular basis throughout the day and this runaround makes it an unnecessary PITA.

I tried soft resets, hard resets and nothing clears the problem.  Trying to get help from Sony is a joke as you are supposed to be able to do this via the Sony Support App which seems to have written to intentionally make it impossible. Trustpilot reviews mirror my findings and Sony don’t even seem to monitor the complaints.  This is the most expensive setup I have ever owned but the audio is now all bricked by poor software and no viable hard reset available.  The App does not even mirror what options you have so having forced me onto a useless App it doesn’t have all the correct buttons or instructions.
Sony you are evading your responsibility to properly support customers who have supported you with high ticket purchases.
I need support and possibly a Technician reset or software that will completely default my sound accessories and install an upgrade that works.

reviews.text: I bought WF-1000XM6 for my mother as a gift, we were messing around with settings and we tried to check out the feature that silences the earpieces when someone is talking. Well, fatal mistake I guess, because even after turning the feature off in the app, which claims that it is off, every time so much as a whisper is detected they shut off permanently until you fiddle with the physical tap controls on the actual device. Tried turning it on and off again, didn’t work, and the voice detection is so sensitive that the pair of earbuds is now more or less unusable except in complete silence, so that’s an over 300 dollar pair of genuinely really nice hardware turned into a paperweight by someone’s poorly programmed software. reviews.title: App is Lacking Key Features
reviews.text: This app really is just bloatware with no real functionality outside of adjusting the sound equalizer setting: which is something that can now be done universally for all your devices in a different app. What this app needs, is to include a widget so that you can interact with your headphones when your phone is locked rather than having to unlock, go into the app, adjust your settings, and then back out. But then again you can always just tap your headphones: but that can be finicky. Widgets work more effectively to get your device to do what it wants without having to go through all the fuss. Again, until they have a widget, you just won’t be using this app outside of updates 🤷‍♀️🤷

reviews.title: Missing the mark
reviews.text: I hate that when I open the app, most of the screen is filled with an image of the headphones I’m wearing. I have never opened the app to find out what my headphones look like or what the model number is. Put that info elsewhere. What I do want when I open the app, the overwhelming majority of the time, is to access the equalizer and/or the connected devices. It’s obnoxious that I have to scroll for that, when it could easily fit on my screen direct from clicking to open the app if there wasn’t a giant image of the expensive headphones I already own taking up all the space. In fact, the only button on my screen without scrolling is a feature I can control with a physical button on the headphones! Put it elsewhere, or let me re-arrange the features. I could also rant about the other weird choices regarding how the app is organized, but I’d rather focus on what’s explicitly irritating — like not being able to switch between the two devices the headphones can connect to. The only way to switch is for the current device playing sound to completely stop. So if I’m playing a game on my laptop, walk away, and my phone rings — there’s no way to answer my phone without running back and closing the game I was playing or disconnecting the bluetooth connection to my laptop and having the game audio blast out of it, while I try to answer my phone. Why can’t I just switch devices from the app?? I honestly sometimes feel this app was made via an AI prompt or something. Terrible interface.
